messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Problems with longer iterations in Mixture Model
parts:
On Monday, March 20, 2017 at 9:57:16 AM UTC-4, smockin morry wrote:
Where could be the problem, model specification?  Kindly help.

My guess is that this in generated quantities:

generated quantities {
  matrix[N, k_groups] p;
  for (n in 1:N){
    vector[k_groups] ps;
    for (K in 1:k_groups){
      ps[K] = theta[K]*exp(normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[K], sigma));
    }
    for (k in 1:k_groups){
      p[n, k]=ps[k]/sum(ps);
    }
  }
}

the last line overflows to infinity / infinity. You would be better off doing

ps[K] = log(theta[K]) + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[K], sigma);

and then

p[n, ] = transpose(softmax(ps));

Ben

Thanks Masschelein for the response.

 I have already implemented one of the resolutions, that is by enforcing the ordering of means of components in the model as  suggested 
by Michael in the link you provided. Just to understand where the problem could be, i have changed Michael's  binary mixture model to a general mixture model as 
provided in the Stan manual  and both approaches provides similar estimates of parameters as shown below. 
But the problem of label identification seems apparent to a general mixture model when
 the number of components K is greater than 2 as shown below. 
1. Does it mean that solutions to label switching only works in a binary mixture model?  
2. How can the general mixture model be tweaked to avoid label switching menace when is say K>3

Binary mixture model approach

binary_mix_ordered<-"
data {
 int<lower = 0> N;
 vector[N] y;
}

parameters {
  ordered[2] mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma[2];
  real<lower=0, upper=1> theta;
}

model {
 sigma ~ normal(0, 2);
 mu ~ normal(0, 2);
 theta ~ beta(5, 5);
for (n in 1:N)

target += log_mix(theta,
                     normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[1], sigma[1]),
                     normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[2], sigma[2]));
}"
